title: A factory that wastes nothing
description:
Write two helpers that construct objects in place, forwarding every argument perfectly so that nothing is copied on the way.

- `make<T>(args...)`: returns a `std::unique_ptr<T>` built from the arguments. This is essentially `std::make_unique`.
- `emplaceBack(vector, args...)`: constructs a new element at the end of a `std::vector<T>` from the arguments and returns a reference to it.

Both take a parameter pack of forwarding references (`Args&&... args`) and expand it with `std::forward<Args>(args)...`.

The tests use a type that counts how often it is copied. Passing a temporary through your helpers must cause **zero** copies.
hints: `template <typename T, typename... Args> std::unique_ptr<T> make(Args&&... args) { return std::unique_ptr<T>{ new T(std::forward<Args>(args)...) }; }`.
`emplaceBack` forwards the same way into `vector.emplace_back(std::forward<Args>(args)...)`, which returns a reference to the new element (C++17).
